label: Empty State
title: Empty State
summary: Use an Empty State when a list or screen has nothing to show, to say why and offer one next step.
corePrinciple: Say what’s missing, then what to do next.

sizing.title: As wide as its container, as tall as its content
sizing.description: Empty State takes its width from its container and centres its text. It has 4 px of padding, 16 px between the icon, title, and description, and 24 px above the button. Figma’s version is 236 px wide.

content.title: What’s missing, why, and what next
content.description: Write the title as what’s missing, in a few words. Use the description for why it’s empty or what will appear, and label the button with the next step. Empty State has no copy of its own and shows a button only when you give it a label, so set all three.

sources.title: Use the public Empty State contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (23 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Empty state is one 236 px component with a red 81 px icon and a 32 px button. The package has no copy of its own and shows a button only when given a label or an action; passing null removes the icon or the button. Its modes reach the icon and button you pass in, and their own modes win. It has no background, so this page shows Light only. On the web a titled Empty State is a region named by its title, which is a heading. Its default icon is hidden from screen readers, but an icon you pass in is read as an unnamed image. The published Storybook predates this build.
